([[White Plains, New York]]) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2021–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 16 | draft_team = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | career_start = 2022 | career_end = 2024 | career_number = 14 | career_position = [[Small forward]] | years1 = {{nbay|2022|start}}–{{nbay|2023|end}} | team1 = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team2 = →[[College Park Skyhawks]] | highlights = * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman Team (2022) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2021]]) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|the {{USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|FIBA Americas U16 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship|2019 Brazil]]|[[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|Team]]}} | stats_league = NBA | stat1label = [[Point (basketball)|Points]] | stat1value = 687 (7.5 ppg) | stat2label = [[Rebound (basketball)|Rebounds]] | stat2value = 171 (1.9 rpg) | stat3label = [[Assist (basketball)|Assists]] | stat3value = 78 (0.8 apg) }} '''Adrian Darnell''' "'''AJ'''" '''Griffin Jr.''' (born August 25, 2003) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who spent two seasons with the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) before abruptly retiring, citing his [[religious faith]]. He was a first-round draft pick who played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. ==High school career== Griffin was a starter on the varsity basketball team for [[Ossining High School]] in [[Ossining, New York]], as a seventh- and eighth-grader in 2015–16 alongside senior and future NBA player [[Obi Toppin]].{{Cite web |title=Ossining Basketball Roster (2015-16) - MaxPreps.com |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/ny/ossining/ossining-pride/basketball/15-16/roster/ |access-date=April 25, 2025 |website=MaxPreps.com}} Griffin played basketball for [[Archbishop Stepinac High School]] in [[White Plains, New York]].{{cite web |last=Marks |first=Brendan |title=A.J. Griffin is primed to be another in a long line of Duke stars |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1740404/2020/04/13/a-j-griffin-is-primed-to-be-another-in-a-long-line-of-duke-stars/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=April 13, 2020}} As a freshman, he played with his older brother, [[Alan Griffin (basketball)|Alan]], and helped his team win its first [[Catholic High School Athletic Association]] (CHSAA) Archdiocesan title since 1984.{{cite web |last=Thomson |first=Josh |title=Boys basketball: Griffin brothers lead Stepinac to Archdiocesan title |url=https://www.lohud.com/story/sports/high-school/lohud-varsity-insider/2018/02/24/boys-basketball-griffin-brothers-lead-stepinac-archdiocesan-title/357725002/ |website=[[The Journal News]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=February 24, 2018}} In his sophomore season, he and [[R. J. Davis]] formed one of the top backcourts in the nation.{{cite web |last=McLamb |first=Michael |title=Archbishop Stepinac finds new life with dynamic duo |url=https://www.marsreel.com/archbishop-stepinac-finds-new-life-with-help-from-dynamic-duo/ |website=Mars Reel |access-date=June 18, 2021 |date=February 13, 2019}} Griffin averaged 20.9 points, 10.9 rebounds, 3.9 assists, and 3.5 blocks per game.{{cite web |last=Drumwright |first=Steve |title=AJ Griffin Hopes Continued Improvement in His Game Results in U16 National Team Spot |url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2019/05/aj-griffin-feature.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190524163137/https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2019/05/aj-griffin-feature.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 24, 2019 |website=[[USA Basketball]] |publisher=Red Line Editorial |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=May 24, 2019}} As a junior, he averaged 17.7 points, 8.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 2.3 blocks per game, missing most of the season with a knee injury, and led Stepinac to the CHSAA Archdiocesan title. Griffin was sidelined for his senior season by an ankle injury.{{cite web |last=Thomson |first=Josh |title=Boys basketball: Stepinac's Adrian Griffin Jr., a Duke commit, may not return for senior season |url=https://www.lohud.com/story/sports/high-school/varsity-insider/2021/02/09/boys-basketball-duke-commit-adrian-griffin-jr-may-not-play-2021/4450027001/ |website=[[The Journal News]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=February 9, 2021}} He was named to the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]] rosters.{{cite web |last=Krest |first=Shawn |title=Duke Signees Paolo Banchero, A.J. Griffin Named McDonald's All-Americans |url=https://www.si.com/college/duke/basketball/paolo-banchero-aj-griffin-duke-mcdonalds-all-americans |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=February 26, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Griffin was rated a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports]], [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and [[On3.com|On3]], and a four-star recruit by [[ESPN]].{{cite web |last=Watson |first=John |title=The curious case of AJ Griffin and ESPN's rankings |url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/Article/The-curious-case-of-AJ-Griffin-and-ESPNs-rankings-164502577/ |website=[[247Sports]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=April 21, 2021}} On November 4, 2019, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] over offers from [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] and [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]].{{cite web |last=Jordan |first=Jason |title=2021 Chosen 25 wing A.J. Griffin commits to Duke |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/acc/2019/11/04/2021-chosen-25-wing-aj-griffin-commits-to-duke/40543607/ |website=[[USA Today]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 team|Lafayette]].{{cite news |title=Wendell Moore Jr. heats up as No. 7 Duke beats Lafayette |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401369854 |access-date=December 9, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 19, 2021}} He was named to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman Team as well as Honorable Mention All-ACC.{{cite press release |url=https://theacc.com/news/2022/3/6/athlete-awards-acc-unveils-2021-22-mens-basketball-awards.aspx |title=ACC Unveils 2021–22 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] |date=March 7, 2022 |access-date=March 8, 2022}} At the conclusion of his freshman season, Griffin announced his intention to enter the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |last=Beard |first=Aaron |date=April 24, 2022 |title=Blue Devils' Griffin becomes 5th Duke player to bolt for NBA |url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-sports-march-madness-mens-college-basketball-5651076eb5a13ded090a37cd8656c272 |access-date=April 25, 2025 |website=AP News |language=en}} Ahead of the draft, Griffin was projected as a potential top-five pick.{{Cite web |title=Adrian Griffin Jr. |url=https://nbadraftroom.com/p/adrian-griffin-jr |access-date=April 27, 2022 |website=NBA Draft Room |language=en-US}} ==Professional career== Griffin was selected with the 16th overall pick by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. He later joined the Hawks' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] team.{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612737/hawks|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 20, 2022}} On July 3, 2022, the Hawks signed Griffin to a rookie-scale contract.{{cite web |date=July 3, 2022 |title=Atlanta Hawks Sign First-Round Pick AJ Griffin |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-first-round-pick-aj-griffin |access-date=July 20, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On November 19, Griffin put up 17 points, alongside a game-winning alley-oop, five rebounds, an assist, a steal, and a block in a 124–122 win over the [[2022–23 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web |last=Villas |first=Rexwell |date=November 19, 2022 |title=AJ Griffin saves the day for Hawks with game-winning alley-oop in wild finish vs. Raptors |url=https://clutchpoints.com/hawks-news-aj-griffin-saves-day-game-winning-alley-oop-raptors |access-date=November 19, 2022 |website=ClutchPoints.com}} On December 11, Griffin scored another game-winning alley-oop in a 123–122 win over the [[2022–23 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web |last=Salao |first=R.P. |date=December 11, 2022 |title=VIDEO: Hawks' AJ Griffin hits absurd 180 game-winner with 0.5 left to down Bulls |url=https://clutchpoints.com/hawks-news-aj-griffin-hits-absurd-180-game-winner-with-0-5-left-to-down-bulls |access-date=December 11, 2022 |website=ClutchPoints.com}} On June 27, 2024, the Hawks traded Griffin to the [[Houston Rockets]] for the draft rights of [[Nikola Đurišić]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web |date=June 27, 2024 |title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Draft Rights to Nikola Djurisic |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-draft-rights-to-nikola-djurisic |access-date=June 28, 2024 |website=NBA.com}} However, on September 20, the Rockets and he agreed to a contract buyout{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Luke |date=September 20, 2024 |title=Rockets Reach Buyout Agreement With AJ Griffin |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/rockets-reach-buyout-agreement-with-aj-griffin.html |access-date=September 22, 2024 |website=HoopsRumors.com}} just as he was considering a retirement from basketball.{{cite web |last=Peters |first=Andrew |date=September 20, 2024 |title=NBA Rumors: A.J. Griffin, Rockets Agree to Contract Buyout amid Retirement Buzz |URL=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10136187-nba-rumors-aj-griffin-rockets-agree-to-contract-buyout-amid-retirement-buzz |access-date=September 20, 2024 |website=syndication.bleacherreport.com}}{{cite web |last=Kimble |first=Kade |date=September 20, 2024 |title=Rockets Forward Steps Away From Basketball, Waived by Team |url=https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/news/houston-rockets-forward-steps-away-from-basketball-waived-by-team-aj-griffin |access-date=September 20, 2024 |website=SI.com}}{{cite web |last=Quinn |first=Sam |date=September 13, 2024 |title=Former first-round pick A.J. Griffin considering stepping away from basketball, per report |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/former-first-round-pick-a-j-griffin-considering-stepping-away-from-basketball-per-report/ |access-date=September 20, 2024 |website=CBSSports.com}} ==Retirement== On September 29, 2024, Griffin confirmed his retirement and stated that he "gave up basketball to follow [[Jesus]]". Griffin noted that he wanted to pursue full-time [[Christian ministry]].{{cite web |last=Ward-Henninger |first=Colin |date=September 29, 2024 |title=Former NBA first-round pick A.J. Griffin explains why he 'gave up basketball to follow Jesus' |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/former-nba-first-round-pick-a-j-griffin-explains-why-he-gave-up-basketball-to-follow-jesus/ |access-date=September 29, 2024 |website=CBSSports.com}} ==National team career== Griffin represented the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in Brazil. He averaged 13.5 points, 4.3 rebounds and 3.3 steals per game, helping his team win the gold medal.{{cite web |title=Adrian Griffin (USA)'s profile – FIBA U16 Americas Championship 2019 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/u16americas/2019/player/Adrian-Griffin |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=June 18, 2021}} Griffin scored 18 points against [[Canada men's national under-17 basketball team|Canada]] in the final.{{cite web |last=Giles |first=Matt |title=Gifted 15-year-old treasures Duke basketball offer, plans to visit |url=https://balldurham.com/2019/06/29/duke-basketball-offer-plans-visit/ |website=Ball Durham |access-date=June 18, 2021 |date=June 29, 2019}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} Christian and often takes to social media to speak about his faith.{{cite web |last=Doering |first=Joshua |title=Freshman AJ Griffin boldly living as follower of Christ while leading Duke to Final Four |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/basketball/2022/03/29/aj-griffin-follower-christ-duke-final-four/ |website=Sports Spectrum |date=March 29, 2022 |access-date=April 2, 2022}} Griffin's father, [[Adrian Griffin|Adrian]], played in the NBA for ten seasons before becoming a coach in the league, and served as head coach for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. His mother, Audrey Sterling, was an All-American in [[track and field|track]] and ran for [[Seton Hall Pirates|Seton Hall]]. His oldest sister is Vanessa. His other two siblings have played college basketball: his brother, [[Alan Griffin (basketball)|Alan]], at [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] and [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], and his sister, [[Aubrey Griffin|Aubrey]], at [[UConn Huskies women's basketball|UConn]].{{cite web |last=Waters |first=Mike |title=Meet the Griffins: How family helped shape Alan, Syracuse basketball's exciting newcomer |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2020/11/meet-the-griffins-how-family-helped-shape-alan-syracuse-basketballs-exciting-newcomer.html |website=[[The Post-Standard]] |access-date=December 16, 2020 |date=November 13, 2020}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{basketball stats}} *[https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/aj-griffin/17231 Duke Blue Devils bio] *[https://www.usab.com/players/aj-griffin USA Basketball bio] {{2022 NBA draft}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Griffin, AJ}} [[Category:2003 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Archbishop Stepinac High School alumni]] [[Category:Atlanta Hawks draft picks]] [[Category:Atlanta Hawks players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Dallas]] [[Category:Basketball players from Westchester County, New York]] [[Category:College Park Skyhawks players]] [[Category:Duke Blue Devils men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Small forwards]]
